Pre-primary and early childhood frameworks grounded in human rights principles that prioritize equity, non-discrimination, holistic child well-being, and universal access to safe and inclusive educational environments.

An outcomes-funded early childhood education program model designed to expand access to quality, play-based pre-primary learning for young children living in remote, low-income, and marginalized communities.

Institutional policies, regulatory frameworks, and monitoring mechanisms established to evaluate performance, maintain professional standards, and ensure educational institutions and personnel fulfill their operational and pedagogical responsibilities.
The regular, scheduled physical presence and ongoing participation of an enrolled student in educational activities and classroom instruction at a formal learning institution.
The degree of an enrolled learner's active, sustained emotional, cognitive, and behavioral involvement in academic activities, co-curricular programs, and the broader educational community.

The formal administrative registration and official admission of eligible children into an educational institution, granting them legitimate access to organized instruction and school-based support services.

Integrated school-based interventions, services, and educational strategies that address learners' physical well-being, dietary needs, disease prevention, and hygiene practices to support healthy development and effective learning.

A collaborative, strategic roadmap formulated by school leaders, educators, and community stakeholders that identifies educational priorities, targets resource allocation, and outlines targeted actions to enhance institutional performance and student learning.

An organized institutional or digital framework designed to manage school operations, administrative processes, resource allocation, and decision-making to support effective educational leadership and delivery.
The measurable academic achievement, learning progress, and developmental outcomes of students within primary and foundational education grades.

The foundational cognitive, social-emotional, physical, and early literacy and numeracy competencies that prepare young children to successfully transition into and participate in formal primary education.

term: School-Based Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) Services
definition: Specialized communication supports, strategies, and assistive technologies delivered directly within educational settings to help young children with severe speech or language impairments communicate and participate in learning.

Collaborative governance bodies composed of community members, parents, and educators that oversee school administration, promote safe and inclusive learning environments, and strengthen community support for education.

A professional development approach providing continuous, on-site instructional coaching, feedback, and peer guidance to teachers within their own educational settings to improve pedagogical quality and learning outcomes.

term: Science of Early Childhood Development (SECD) Facilitator
definition: A trained specialist who delivers evidence-based educational content and guidance on early child development research to practitioners, caregivers, and stakeholders working across the early childhood sector.
An evidence-based body of interdisciplinary research that explains how individuals learn to read and informs structured instructional practices to build foundational literacy skills.
The systematic process of assessing young children to detect developmental delays, disabilities, or special learning needs early, facilitating timely referrals and targeted intervention services.

Standardized instruments, checklists, or assessment questionnaires used to systematically evaluate children's developmental progress and detect potential delays, disabilities, or learning difficulties.

Consistent and emotionally responsive caregivers who provide young children with safety, emotional stability, and reassurance, fostering trust, positive socio-emotional development, and confident exploration of their environment.

Educational methods and arrangements that isolate or separate learners with disabilities or specific learning needs from mainstream classrooms, contrasting with inclusive pedagogies that integrate all children.

An educational approach in which children take initiative, make choices, and guide their own exploration and discovery through hands-on activities, fostering autonomy, curiosity, and intrinsic motivation.

The neurological process by which the brain receives, organizes, and responds to sensory information from the body and the environment, supporting functional development and purposeful learning activities in early childhood.
The provision of diverse sensory experiences through sight, sound, touch, and movement within learning environments to actively engage a young child's senses and support overall brain development.

An early literacy skill and activity where learners identify and arrange narrative events or illustrations in logical, chronological order, strengthening comprehension, storytelling ability, and critical thinking.
The use of digital or interactive games intentionally designed for educational purposes, curriculum delivery, and skill development rather than purely for entertainment.

Structured educational instruction that equips individuals with the linguistic fluency, practical skills, and professional ethics needed to facilitate effective, accurate communication between spoken and sign languages.

Advocacy, policy, and educational efforts aimed at increasing awareness, wider institutional adoption, teaching, and formal recognition of sign language to ensure accessible communication for deaf and hard-of-hearing learners.

An instructional strategy where learners are divided into smaller clusters to collaborate, engage in targeted activities, and receive focused teacher interaction, particularly useful for managing large classrooms.

Public and community-based policies and initiatives designed to shield vulnerable households and children from poverty, social exclusion, and economic shocks to support holistic development and wellbeing.

The foundational abilities and behavioral skills that enable children to understand and manage emotions, build healthy relationships, show empathy, and make responsible decisions within learning environments.

A child's understanding of emotions, social rules, and interpersonal dynamics necessary to navigate peer interactions, self-regulate, and participate effectively in early learning and school environments.
Hands-on learning tools and play materials designed to produce auditory feedback, supporting young learners' sensory development, phonological awareness, and interactive exploration through sound.
The foundational literacy practice of pronouncing the individual phonetic sounds associated with specific written letters to bridge letter recognition and early word decoding.

The reciprocal exchange of technical knowledge, successful practices, and policy solutions among low- and middle-income countries to address shared developmental and educational challenges collaboratively.

Specialized instructional techniques, classroom accommodations, and individualized interventions designed to meet the unique learning and developmental needs of children with disabilities or specific learning difficulties.
A specialized clinical and educational intervention that diagnoses and treats communication, language comprehension, expressive speech, and oral motor difficulties in young children.

An active pedagogical approach that integrates physical activities, movement, and structured games into educational programming to promote foundational cognitive skills, inclusion, and positive social development.

An educational framework structured around developmental levels and mastery of specific milestones rather than rigid chronological age or standardized academic grades, accommodating diverse learner capabilities.
Systematic, validated assessment instruments used to identify developmental delays or track progress in children across motor, cognitive, language, and socio-emotional developmental domains.

An instructional framework organized around clear, explicitly defined learning outcomes and developmental benchmarks that specify what young learners are expected to know and demonstrate at each level.

An educational strategy that focuses on identifying, valuing, and building upon learners' inherent abilities and existing competencies rather than concentrating solely on deficits or developmental challenges.
Tangible, input-level aspects of an early childhood learning environment, including physical infrastructure, teacher-child ratios, classroom safety, material resources, and educator qualifications.
Systematically organized educational materials, guides, and learning aids designed to support instructional delivery and scaffold progressive skill development in foundational literacy and numeracy.

The systematic design of step-by-step teaching plans that organize learning objectives, instructional activities, timing, and assessment strategies to ensure coherent curriculum delivery in the classroom.
Instructional materials, such as scripted guides and activity plans, designed to provide educators with explicit, step-by-step support for delivering targeted foundational learning activities.

An evidence-based, explicit, and systematic approach to reading instruction grounded in the science of reading, focusing sequentially on phonological awareness, decoding, phonics, and language comprehension.

Coordinated educational interventions that deliver systematic, evidence-based reading instruction and engaging practice activities to develop foundational reading skills and foster positive reading habits.

An intentional educational approach combining guided play with specific developmental learning objectives, allowing young children to explore and acquire foundational skills in an engaging, supportive environment.

Guided, sequenced instructional exercises and literacy tasks designed to systematically build children's reading comprehension, fluency, and foundational literacy skills through active engagement with texts.

Learners who encounter persistent difficulties in acquiring foundational literacy skills, such as decoding, fluency, or comprehension, and require differentiated instructional support to reach grade-level reading proficiency.

Curriculum-aligned consumable learning materials containing targeted exercises, activities, and practice tasks designed for children to complete independently or with guidance to reinforce foundational concepts.

Periodic on-site monitoring and mentoring sessions conducted by trainers or instructional leaders to observe classroom practices, provide actionable feedback, and reinforce newly acquired teaching skills.

A collaborative and continuous mentoring approach in which education officials or supervisors offer constructive feedback, hands-on guidance, and problem-solving assistance to educators in their classrooms.

A structured method of literacy instruction that teaches learners to link individual letters or letter groups to specific speech sounds and blend them sequentially to pronounce and decode written words.

Comprehensive transformation of an education sector that simultaneously aligns governance, institutional policies, curriculum, and pedagogical practices to achieve sustainable, sector-wide improvements in learning outcomes.
Specific, evidence-based instructional strategies or remediation programs implemented to address identified learning gaps and meet the unique academic needs of particular groups of learners.
The total number of children enrolled in pre-primary education, regardless of age, expressed as a percentage of the official school-age population corresponding to that level.

Specialized instructional mentors who provide educators with direct, ongoing professional development, pedagogical guidance, and classroom-based modeling to improve teaching practices and learning outcomes.
The specific set of professional knowledge, pedagogical skills, and personal attributes that educators need to effectively facilitate child development and foundational learning.

Formal policies, coursework, and practical training programmes designed to equip prospective and practicing educators with the professional knowledge and pedagogical skills necessary for classroom teaching.
An explicit instructional technique where an educator directly demonstrates a task, thought process, or learning behavior to scaffold understanding before students attempt it independently.
The pre-service training, academic coursework, and practical field experiences designed to qualify and equip candidate educators before they assume full professional teaching responsibilities.

A measure of educator effectiveness encompassing academic qualifications, subject mastery, pedagogical competence, and professional classroom practices that drive meaningful student learning and development.

Continuous institutional, professional, and pedagogical assistance provided to educators through mentoring, coaching, instructional feedback, and resources to strengthen their classroom performance and well-being.

A formal framework specifying the learning objectives, pedagogical competencies, instructional content, and assessment criteria designed to prepare or upskill educators in professional teaching practices.
Low-cost, locally sourced educational aids and learning manipulatives crafted directly by educators to supplement standard kits and make classroom instruction more contextually relevant.
The practical pedagogical abilities, instructional techniques, and classroom management competencies that educators apply to foster positive learning environments and deliver effective instruction.
Purposeful instructional methods, plans, and pedagogical approaches adopted by educators to facilitate comprehension, engage learners, and achieve defined learning and developmental outcomes.

Specialized professional expertise, advisory support, and capacity-building services provided to educational institutions, governments, or practitioners to enhance the design, implementation, and quality of learning systems and programs.

A multi-level professional support framework that cascades coaching and instructional guidance across three distinct tiers, such as master trainers, school-based coaches, and classroom teachers, to systematically reinforce pedagogical skills.

A community resource center or lending service that provides children, caregivers, and early childhood educators with shared access to developmentally appropriate toys, games, and learning materials to promote play-based development.

Culturally rooted or indigenous play-based activities and counting games that leverage local traditions to foster foundational numeracy, logical reasoning, and social-emotional skills in young children.

The coordinated planning, policy guidelines, and support processes designed to ensure young children experience smooth, continuous, and developmentally appropriate progression between early childhood care centers and formal primary schooling.

Structured institutional processes, curricular alignments, and collaborative practices established between early childhood centers and primary schools to support continuous learning, readiness, and successful student adjustment.

An educational provision policy or initiative that eliminates direct enrollment and instructional fees, enabling all children, particularly those from marginalized or vulnerable backgrounds, to access foundational schooling without financial barriers.

An African philosophical approach to teaching and learning rooted in interconnectedness, communal values, and mutual respect, which fosters inclusive, relational, and culturally responsive early learning environments.

Child-directed, open-ended play that lacks adult-imposed rules or prescribed outcomes, allowing young learners to freely explore their environment, exercise autonomy, and cultivate creativity and problem-solving skills.

Instructional resources such as charts, posters, flashcards, diagrams, and realia that use visual stimuli to reinforce foundational concepts, stimulate language development, and enhance comprehension in early childhood classrooms.
The ability to coordinate visual perception with fine motor movements, enabling children to translate visual information into physical actions such as drawing, writing, and manipulating objects.
Young people at heightened risk of social, educational, or physical harm due to conditions such as extreme poverty, chronic illness, orphanhood, exploitation, or systemic marginalisation.

A standardised screening questionnaire designed to identify children experiencing functional difficulties across multiple developmental domains, including vision, hearing, mobility, communication, learning, and social interaction.
A severe form of acute malnutrition characterized by a rapid, dangerous loss of weight relative to height, typically resulting from acute food shortages or recurrent illness.
Educational spaces and pedagogical practices structured around the developmental needs, interests, and active participation of learners, encouraging play, inquiry, and collaborative discovery.
A decentralized administrative and pedagogical district responsible for the supervision, monitoring, and operational support of pre-primary and primary schools within a designated geographic area.

term: Early Childhood Development and Family Centre
definition: An integrated community facility providing comprehensive early education, healthcare, nutrition, and psychosocial support services to young children while offering parenting guidance and resources to families.
aliases: early childhood development and family centres

definition: The gradual process through which young children learn to recognize, understand, express, and regulate their feelings while developing empathy and forming meaningful relationships with others.
The learned abilities to identify, express, and regulate one’s own feelings effectively, cope with stress, and respond with empathy to the emotions of peers and adults.

Policies, programmes, and pedagogical practices dedicated to ensuring equitable access, safe participation, retention, and quality learning outcomes for female children across all levels of schooling.
The gradual growth and coordination of large muscle groups and whole-body movements essential for balance, posture, running, jumping, and general physical mobility during early childhood.
Formal residential care provided to children in non-family, structured group facilities such as orphanages, often utilized when family-based alternatives or parental care are unavailable.
The specific language designated and utilized for instructing children in foundational reading, writing, and communication skills within formal or informal early learning environments.
An instructional approach where children are taught early academic concepts and foundational literacy in their primary home language before transitioning to additional or official national languages.

A temporary, flexible early childcare service established in community spaces, workplaces, or emergency contexts to provide safe supervision, nurturing care, and early learning opportunities for young children.
Formal educational coursework and practical pedagogical preparation completed by aspiring educators at training institutions before they begin professional teaching in classrooms.
An adult who consistently observes, accurately interprets, and sensitively reacts to a young child's communicative, physical, and emotional cues to foster secure attachment and healthy development.
Guidance, nurturing practices, and structured interactions designed to help children recognize and regulate emotions, build positive relationships, develop empathy, and navigate social environments.
Structured instructional tasks, guided play, and interactive exercises facilitated by educators to help children acquire, practice, and master foundational knowledge, skills, and competencies.
The cognitive processes and mental strategies that enable children to process information, reason, solve problems, make decisions, and reflect critically on their learning.
